target_customer: Affluent households buying a home robot, with reservations open from October 2026
problem: Household tidying is a constant chore that existing robots like vacuums do not address. Tuesday Labs is building Voxel, a legged home robot that tidies, finds items and tends plants.
business_model: Hardware sales with refundable 200 dollar reservations and an expected price near 20,000 dollars, deliveries targeted for 2028

founders.name: Rosalind (Ros) Shinkle
prior_employers: Boston Dynamics (Staff Robotics Engineer, Spot Manipulation team)
education: UPenn, BSE in Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics

competitors.name: Samsung Bot Handy
competitors.what: Concept home robot with an arm to tidy, load a dishwasher and set the table
competitors.traction_then: Concept shown at CES, no product

technical_complexity.rationale: General household manipulation by a legged robot is research-grade, and the company says the prototype is a concept whose hardware may be substantially redesigned.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and learned manipulation skill could become a moat if solved, but at this stage nothing shipped and well funded humanoid developers are targeting the same task.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large firms showed concepts and demos (Samsung Bot Handy, Dyson prototypes, Figure) but none shipped a consumer tidying robot by late 2026.

market_need_then: Home chores are a broad pain point, robot vacuums proved households pay for automation, and 2023 to 2024 progress in learned manipulation revived interest in general home robots.

identity.mascot_or_character: Voxel robot, with its eyes in the belly and no head, personality shaped with animators according to press
identity.visual_style: Playful design drawing on lamps, chairs and briefcases per founder comments to Dezeen
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful and irreverent taglines such as MAKE A MESS and LET IT BE

branding.brand_signature: Voxel's headless, expressive character design with a warm, playful tone

rebrands.why: Not stated; aggregators say the company later pivoted to home robots

branding.community_and_virality: Voxel launch in October 2026 drew coverage from Dezeen, Interesting Engineering, Notebookcheck and others

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive playful voice and character design drew design and tech press at the October 2026 reveal, but no shipping product or measurable community yet.

pivots.from: Remote human assistance for autonomous robots (Adagy Robotics, per aggregators)

outcome_analysis: Tuesday Labs is active and pre-revenue, after unveiling the Voxel Series-1 prototype in October 2026 with refundable reservations and 2028 delivery targets. The sources do not support success or failure judgments yet. The venture needs a large hardware raise, and its funding outside a small early round is not public.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators list a 500K pre-seed dated 2024-04-03 with YC, Fellows Fund, FundersClub and Ludlow Ventures, while others give no amount or a Jan 2025 date. Founding year differs (2023 on YC page, 2025 in Dezeen). The Adagy Robotics origin comes from aggregators only. Company site says venture-backed. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed rests on a single database (Extruct); Seedtable labels it a seed on 2024-04-01 with no amount.
